examples.knowledge_point: Computing Limits of Piecewise Functions with a Gap in the Domain
examples.problem:
Find $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1}g(x)$ for the function given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+5}}{3x-7}\, & \text{ for }\,x\le 1 \\ (x-2)^{2}-1\, & \text{ for }\,x\ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute $\lim\limits_{x \to \, 1} g(x),$ we must compute the left and right-sided limits separately.

However, the right-sided limit $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^+}g(x)$ does not exist since $g(x)$ is not defined in the interval $x\in(1,2).$ 

Consequently, the overall limit does not exist either:

$$
\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1}g(x) = \text{DNE}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the left-sided limit at $x=4$ for the function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x} & \text{ for }\,0\le x<4 \\ 2 & \text{ for }\,x=4 \\ \sqrt{x-2} & \text{ for }\,x>4.\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<4,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{x}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\sqrt{x} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
